DISCARDED: the max-F-rephrase instrument (rewrite the tag to be 'max of this facet', embed-compare) — rewrite-distance conflates incidental wording change + topic leak + the actual facet change; tracks surface variation more than the attribute. Replaced by query-time clustering (the prompt's own facet phrase is the live cluster center; no rewrite, no probe, no rewrite-distance).

DISCARDED: SpLiCE / sparse-code-over-dictionary (NN-LASSO over a fixed concept dictionary) — the lean-graph reframe moved graded facets to query-time; there's no baked per-facet coordinate to solve for, and the dictionary would be exactly the bloat the user rejected. Live cosine to the prompt's facet phrase replaces it.

DISCARDED: INSTRUCTOR-conditioning (encoder conditioned per facet, no rewrite) — still bakes a per-facet vector at index time, which the lean-graph reframe rejects. The instruction is also adjacent to the dead cosine(tag, embed('facet')) comparison.

DISCARDED for graded, KEPT (deferred) for categorical: the exemplar-region route (difference-of-means over real F-maximal tags, mined deterministically) — dropped for graded because query-time clustering replaces it; kept for categorical (entity-type via directory join, info-kind via detectors) as baked tag attributes (pass 2).

DISCARDED: 'facet = relevance coordinate' (the 06-14 framing) — routing leaking into the facet definition. Replaced by the guide-link model (06-25): a facet is a concept both tag and prompt are measured-close-to.

DISCARDED: the uniform graded facet vector (v1's 5-vector of [0,1] fit scores, same instrument, same shape) — three measurement natures (categorical / graded / scalar) cannot share one shape; forced them into graded and produced the hollowing (entity-type + info-kind misread as facts and deleted). User's load-bearing cut at t42: 'not all facets should be graded in the same way'.

DISCARDED: baking graded facets at index (the §3 canon: per-facet value = corpus-relative measure, stored as a tag attribute vector) — dropped at t52 when user said 'an optimal solution would to NOT have all of this in the graph, intead do it live-prompt-time, because of the size it's becoming'. Graded facets + corpus-relational weights move to query time; categorical + centrality + embeddings stay baked.

DISCARDED (already dead): per-facet edges (v1 mistake) — one edge per facet carrying that facet's weight. Replaced by one edge per tag carrying the whole relational layer. In the lean-graph build, the edge carries only centrality (deferred); graded weights are query-time.

DISCARDED: the 5-facet v2 set (topic, process, stance, communicative-function, temporal-stance/TAM) — assistant-synthesized, never user-hard-approved; hollowed the tag (every dimension had a cheaper structure-or-interpreter home, so the v2 tag became a bare topic phrase). The content profile (activity, entity-type, information-kind, centrality) replaces it; postures (stance/function/TAM) go to the interpreter.

DISCARDED: hard clustering (hard-assign each tag to its top facet, rank within) — rejected by §14.4 (no hard filters; facets order, never filter). The combinator uses continuous coefficients, not gates. Soft-assign (continuous cosine per facet, weighted sum) = what the design already specifies.

DISCARDED: HNSW / FAISS for the tag embedding index — dropped at t60 when user said 'wtf is this? HNSW (or FAISS)'. At HERB scale (~13,776 tags) exact kNN over a numpy matrix is instant and trivially correct. HNSW/FAISS are for millions of vectors — premature complexity. One matmul, no approximation.

DISCARDED: kNN as the retrieval primitive — at this scale it's a full dot product (tag_matrix @ facet_phrases.T → [n_phrases, n_facets]), every tag gets its facet-weight vector in one shot. kNN would be an optimization to avoid computing the full matrix, but at 13,776 × ~5 the full multiply is cheaper than building an index.

DISCARDED: a relationship layer in the graph (record nodes / relationship edges for multi-hop) — §7 killed it deliberately as the 'copies disease at the node level'. Multi-hop is handled by chunk attributes (ids, kind, product) + references into raw + directory joins + a query-side composition path, not by new nodes.

DISCARDED: 'HERB is mostly single-hop' (assistant's t25 claim) — reversed at t31 after user 'quite alot of multihop, check the HERB documentation instead of asking me'. HERB dataset card: 'Deep Search and Long Context Reasoning... multi-hop questions.' Every gold-100 question is multi-hop; several need aggregation. The artefact is the first-hop retriever; the chain lives in the generator + raw-via-references + directory joins.

CORRECTION t18: 'well, i separate the facets the interpreter use, and the actual real contextual/semantical facets the graph has in it' — assistant had conflated the interpreter's prompt-side decomposition with the graph's corpus-side tag-facets. Fix: re-cut on the correct side — the hard-field apparatus + detectors are corpus-end measurement instruments for the graph-side tag-facets; the interpreter uses the same apparatus's other half (literal flagging) to produce the prompt-end. Symmetry + separation preserved.

CORRECTION t27: 'quite alot of multihop, check the HERB documentation instead of asking me' — assistant had claimed HERB is mostly single-hop. Fix: read the HERB dataset card + gold-100 questions, reverse the claim. HERB is fundamentally a multi-hop + aggregation benchmark; the artefact is the first-hop retriever; the aggregation path is a real design gap.

CORRECTION t39: 'uniform vector? what?' — assistant had characterized the v1 model as a 'uniform facet vector' and argued against it, but the user didn't recognize the framing. Fix: clarify that 'uniform vector' = the v1 5-vector of graded [0,1] fit scores, and that the split (categorical / graded / scalar) is only a reframe if the user was picturing all facets as graded-closeness. User's t42 'not all facets should be graded in the same way' confirms the split lands.

CORRECTION t59: 'wtf is this? HNSW (or FAISS)' — assistant had hedged the ANN choice instead of picking one. Fix: neither — at HERB scale exact kNN over a numpy matrix is instant and trivially correct. Ponytail: pick the simplest thing that works.

CORRECTION t82: 'fs,. i just said it's NEMOTRON FFS!' — assistant had framed the embedder choice as a 'micro-decision' between Nemotron and DESIGN §11's nv-embedqa-1b-v2, even though user had already said 'embedder is nemo' at t81. Fix: Nemotron, settled, no hedge. The assistant's framing of a settled decision as open was the hedge that drew the correction.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY the uniform vector was dropped — three measurement natures cannot share one shape. Entity-type is categorical (measured by directory join, equality-matched). Activity is graded (measured by embedding geometry, cosine-matched). Centrality is a scalar (chunk-local degree, a weight not a facet). The v1 5-vector forced all three into graded [0,1] fit scores and produced the hollowing.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY graded moved to query-time — dissolves three open problems at once: (a) the graded instrument (no probe, no SpLiCE dictionary, no exemplar-region, no max-F rephrase; the prompt's own facet phrase is the live cluster center); (b) axis-definition vs calibration (the axis = the prompt's phrase, live; calibration = a global corpus-relative geometry transform); (c) the no-LLM-judge constraint (the weight is computed live, nothing emitted). Cost: departs from §3 canon for the graded part; user accepted at t52.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY the graph stays lean — the facet layer was becoming a second derived layer inside the graph, exactly the bloat the design rejected elsewhere (§7 killed entity/record nodes for the same reason: copies-not-references). User's t52 'embeddings, values, pointers etc, might be ok' defines the lean graph's content: the spine + tag embeddings + chunk hard-field attributes + references into raw + centrality-on-edge (deferred). Everything facet-related is computed live from the prompt.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY no phrase text in graph nodes — the phrase is the embedding's source, not the retrieval handle. The embedding is the handle; the phrase is re-derivable from the tags jsonl (re-embeddable from there, displayed by joining tag-id → phrases when needed). Consistent with references-not-copies: the phrase is a derived label, the embedding is a derived index, both re-derivable from the chunk + the stateless tagger prompt. User raised at t68; assistant agreed at t69.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY Nemotron — one embedder in the stack gives a fair mechanism comparison between the artefact arm and the vector arm (the comparison is about facets vs dense, not the embedder). User said 'embedder is nemo' at t81, corrected the assistant's hedge at t82. Embedder = nvidia/llama-nemotron-embed-1b-v2, already used in embed_tags.py and the vector arm.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY both DB + in-memory — user wants the Neo4j DB for visual inspection + size ('just do the db for my sake also, i like the visual representation of it and i want to see the size') AND the in-memory structure for the query engine (at HERB scale no benefit to a DB round-trip; the lean graph is a data structure loaded at prepare()). The DB persists for visual inspection; the in-memory structure loads from the npz for speed. User's t81 'remember it's graph-shaped' — tag nodes are real nodes with edges to chunks, not just rows in a matrix.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY the model swap (glm-5.1 → llama-3.3-70b) — NIM was hard-throttling z-ai/glm-5.1 (every call 429s after 6 retries). User skipped the model-choice question at t108, so the assistant made the call: meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct is proven on HERB tagging and on a different NIM per-model clock from glm-5.1, so the throttle shouldn't carry over. The swap is one line (INTERPRETER_MODEL); the contract is model-agnostic.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY the combinator is accumulate-not-max — strong across several relevant facets beats max on one (tagB[func .8, temporal .9]=1.7 beats tagA[func 1.0, temporal .2]=1.2 when both facets relevant). Also why context_precision_id is lower (0.068 vs 0.148) — accumulate + dedupe emits more ids per question, so precision-by-id is diluted. The design showing its hand, not a bug.

CAUSE-AND-EFFECT: WHY no hard filters — a hard filter crushes signal and gates on a JUDGMENT that can be wrong (a true decision mis-tagged 'status' would be silently, totally excluded). 'Mandatory' is achieved by weight concentration, not a gate; the cap does the cutting on the ranked continuum. The structural boost is additive (+1.0), not multiplicative — a multiplicative boost on a zero semantic score would be a hard filter in disguise (§14.4 forbids).
